speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning. To help me understand your double vision and weakness, has this condition been present since birth or did it develop recently?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: That pattern of worsening with activity and improving with rest is classic for myasthenia gravis; has anyone previously diagnosed you with thyroid issues or do you experience dry eyes and dry mouth? REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine_receptor_antibody, Thyroid_function_test.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibodies: Present (elevated); Thyroid_function_test: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The patient's presentation of fatigable weakness worsening with activity and improving with rest, combined with specific diplopia triggered by looking up or down, is pathognomonic for Myasthenia Gravis. The previous suggestion of Tuberculosis is inconsistent with this clinical picture, and I have already ordered the Acetylcholine receptor antibody test and thyroid function tests to confirm the diagnosis and screen for associated autoimmune conditions.
